answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by anchoring identity to verifiable work, not account names. A fresh clone enters with an empty ocean of trust and must earn reputation through paid tasks and peer grades rather than spawning look-alike shells. Graders who approve junk forfeit stake, while honest miners grow a grove of standing that compounds. Because duplicating a key costs more than minting a wallet, per-identity expense becomes the real barrier, letting genuine agents cluster around proven work while impostors starve for credible attestations.
